age.evidence: 4-12 month-old mice (Mus musculus, C57BL/6J, Jackson Laboratories and bred-in house)

sex.evidence: In total, 14 male and 7 female mice were used for this study.

dosing.evidence: DOI (2,5-dimethoxy-4-iodoamphetamine; Sigma, 10mg/kg in saline) or saline (0.9% NaCl) were administered subcutaneously halfway throughout the recording

handling.evidence: Animals were handled by the experimenter for several days before surgical procedures

group_housing.evidence: Mice were housed with sibling cage mates until the beginning of experiments and then they were singly housed.

day_night_flipped.evidence: were kept on a 12-h light/dark cycle (direction/phase of testing not stated)

assays.assay_name: Freely Moving Arena Active Vision (Gaze Shift / Locomotion) Assay
assays.assay_description: Tethered, head-mounted-camera/IMU-equipped mice freely explored a ~48 x 37 x 30 cm arena (visual-stimulus monitor wall, patterned wallpaper, Lego bricks on a silicone mat floor, scattered tortilla chips) for ~45 min before and again after s.c. DOI (10 mg/kg) or saline. Measures: gaze-shift frequency, compensatory movements, head/eye/gaze velocities during gaze shifts, locomotor activity, % time mobile, % time in centre, pupil size. A darkness variant (pilocarpine, ~30 min) was also run in the same arena.

application_type.evidence: Mice were then given a subcutaneous injection of either DOI (10mg/kg in saline) or saline (0.9% NaCl)

setup_habituation.evidence: subsequently habituated (~45 minutes total) to the spherical treadmill and freely moving arena with hardware tethering attached for several days before experiments.

setup_restrain.evidence: animals were first placed in the freely-moving arena which they could explore for 45 minutes

food_restriction.evidence: Small pieces of tortilla chips (Juanita's) were lightly scattered around the arena to encourage foraging during the recording; however, animals were not water or food restricted.

water_restriction.evidence: animals were not water or food restricted. (Presence of water inside the arena is not described.)

time_to_assay.evidence: After waiting 15 minutes, experiments were repeated in reverse order (post-injection head-fixed block of ~30 min preceded the arena), i.e. post-drug arena recording began ~45 min after injection.

sample_size.evidence: we first asked if either DOI (n= 10) or saline (n=4) altered the active sampling behaviors (i.e. gaze shifts) of free-moving mice

outcomes.summary: DOI increased gaze-shift frequency (24.39 to 29.95 per minute; highly variable across mice), whereas saline decreased it (27.38 to 17.46 per minute); the DOI vs saline difference was significant. Head/eye velocity profiles of gaze shifts were unchanged, and DOI's effect on gaze-shift frequency correlated strongly with its effect on locomotion.
outcomes.statistics: Z = 1.98, p = 0.04 (Wilcoxon rank-sum test, DOI vs saline change in gaze shift frequency); Pearson r = 0.89, p = 5.2e-4 (gaze shift frequency change vs locomotion change)
outcomes.evidence: DOI did alter the frequency of gaze shifts, increasing the average number of gaze shifts per minute by 5.56 (± 3.79; from an average of 24.39 gaze shifts/minute before DOI to 29.95 after DOI)... The difference in saline and DOI's effect on gaze shift frequency was significant ( Z = 1.98, p = 0.04; Wilcoxon rank-sum test).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Gaze shift frequency, compensatory movement count, locomotor activity, percentage of time mobile, percentage of time in centre, pupil size (Fig 1E, Fig S1).

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Behaviour compared only as pre- vs post-injection totals/averages; no within-session time course of behaviour reported.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No analysis of transitions or behavioural sequences reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: we focus our analyses on gaze-shifting head and eye movements as those are the natural behaviors which result in new retinal input to the visual system.

B5_social.evidence: Assay measures individual active vision and locomotion; no social component.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Free exploration; no learning or memory requirement.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: eight points around the pupil were tracked with DeepLabCut... The mouse's position in the arena was tracked with DeepLabCut using top-down camera frames.

B8_multivariate.evidence: PCA/k-means applied only to neural PETHs, not to behavioural features.

E1_environment_type.evidence: The floor was a gray silicone mat (Gartful) and was covered with black and white Lego bricks to provide three-dimensional visual contrast. Small pieces of tortilla chips... were lightly scattered around the arena

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter or refuge described in the arena.

E3_bedding.evidence: The floor was a gray silicone mat (Gartful)

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material described in the arena.

E5_enrichment.evidence: covered with black and white Lego bricks to provide three-dimensional visual contrast

E6_spatial.evidence: The arena was approximately 48-cm long by 37-cm wide by 30-cm high

E7_social_context.evidence: Single tethered mouse recorded in the arena; no conspecific described.

E8_food_water.evidence: Small pieces of tortilla chips (Juanita's) were lightly scattered around the arena to encourage foraging during the recording

D1_continuity.evidence: Mice were first placed into the freely-moving arena... for ~45 minutes before being head-fixed... experiments were repeated in reverse order

D2_session_duration.evidence: animals were first placed in the freely-moving arena which they could explore for 45 minutes

D3_recording_days.evidence: In total, recordings took approximately 3 hours.

D4_baseline.evidence: we recorded neural activity in primary visual cortex (V1) of mice during free movement, while simultaneously recording eye and head position, before and after administration

D5_followup.evidence: All recordings within ~3 h session; no recording >=24 h post-drug.

D6_circadian.evidence: In total, recordings took approximately 3 hours.

judge_notes: Dropped deepseek4's 'Head-Fixed Visual Stimulus Assay': its outcomes are V1 neural responses to visual stimuli (electrophysiology), excluded by the rubric; no behavioural outcome was reported for the head-fixed block.
Darkness free-moving recordings are the same arena paradigm under a different condition; folded into the single freely moving assay (their outcomes are neural anyway).
B1: set value '4-6' (score 2); gemma's '2-3' label was inconsistent with its score and the paper reports gaze shifts, compensatory movements, locomotion, time mobile, centre time, and pupil size.
E1: modal 'Enriched arena' (qwen, deepseek) retained given Lego bricks, patterned walls and scattered food; E3: silicone mat not counted as bedding (modal 0).
D2: ~45 min arena session → 15–60 min (score 1); deepseek's 61 min–6 h rejected.
time_to_assay: post-injection arena followed a 15 min wait plus ~30 min head-fixed block (reverse order), so ~45 min (qwen); confidence medium since arena start time is not stated explicitly.
water_restriction: modal 'no' retained from 'animals were not water or food restricted', but water presence inside the arena is not described, so confidence is medium.
